set.body:
Objective:
Close the optional Frame ecosystem phase with an evidence-backed compatibility matrix, documentation, and publication boundaries that preserve independent versioning.

Acceptance:
- Parquet, DuckDB, and Gale adapters each publish an explicit supported type, expression, nullability, ordering, ownership, and platform matrix.
- Adapter differential tests use the local Frame engine as semantic reference and independent format/kernel oracles where internal consistency would be insufficient.
- Explain and action receipts distinguish decoding, borrowing, sharing, rechunking, compaction, packing, copying, spill, and backend segmentation.
- Examples show the same Frame program executed locally and in DuckDB, plus a separate explicit transition through frame-gale.
- Failure examples demonstrate unsupported-plan, closed-buffer, schema mismatch, null-policy, and backend-semantic rejection.
- Optional artifacts can be omitted without changing frame-core behavior or API.
- Versioning and release policy state which modules are stable, experimental, JVM-only, Scala.js-capable, or demand-gated.
- Saved benchmark and memory receipts support every performance claim; no general zero-copy, out-of-core, or backend-equivalence language exceeds the evidence.
set.title: Frame adapters acceptance: conformance matrix, receipts, examples, and release boundaries
